evidence.positive: Boot of the throwaway instance imported the shipped antibiotic-pathways.csv for every tenant: 'Saved 463 antibiotic pathways for tenant TenantKey[value=mayo-mayo]; table holds 463', and 64 each for demo-demo, mgb-mgh, mgb-icsnh. Queried the new tenant tables directly and every notation element came out as documented. For mayo p-cholecystectomy ('CEFAZOLIN -> (CIPROFLOXACIN AND METRONIDAZOLE) OR (CIPROFLOXACIN AND CLINDAMYCIN)') the DB holds step_number 1 option 0 = CEFAZOLIN, step_number 2 option 0 = CIPROFLOXACIN@0 AND METRONIDAZOLE@1, step_number 2 option 1 = CIPROFLOXACIN@0 AND CLINDAMYCIN@1 - '->' became steps, 'OR' became option positions, 'AND' became join rows whose antibiotic_pathway_option_medication_categories.position preserves the file's order, and the parentheses were stripped. 'None' (p-cast-application) became one pathway with no_prophylaxis=t and zero options. Risk and Acuity scope as written: p-pancreatectomy has risk LOW and HIGH pathways at position 0 and 1; p-cesarean-delivery has one pathway scoped ELECTIVE and one scoped EMERGENT|URGENT from the 'urgent | emergent' cell. Then exercised the importer at runtime rather than only at boot: POST /api/admin/config-imports/antibiotic-pathways/upload for demo-demo with a hand-written 5-row file covering three steps, an OR-of-AND-groups step, None, a multi-procedure cell with a piped acuity list, and a LOW/HIGH risk pair returned 200 {recordCountBefore:64, recordCountAfter:6} and the 11 resulting option rows matched the notation cell for cell.
evidence.negative: Uploaded, to the same admin endpoint against the populated demo-demo tenant (64 pathways), a file whose every drug row names a category that does not exist. Response was 500 'Failed to import Antibiotic Pathways: Antibiotic pathway import resolved no medication category across all 2 drug rows for tenant TenantKey[value=demo-demo]; the medication list has not imported', and the tenant still reported recordCount 64 (confirmed independently with select count(*) from "demo-demo".antibiotic_pathways = 64). Repeated with a file carrying the wrong header row: 500 'Antibiotic pathway import read 1 rows and found no Procedure/Pathway pair ...; check the header row', count still 64. Then repeated the same unimportable file on the startup path by overwriting /app/resources/data/org/demo/procedures/antibiotic-pathways.csv inside the container and restarting: boot logged the same IllegalStateException, the app started normally, and demo-demo still held its 64 pathways.
evidence.red_check: Compiled a pre-fix build of AntibioticPathwayCSVImporter in the app container (javac against /app/jib-classpath-file, @Slf4j replaced with an explicit org.slf4j logger since lombok is not on the runtime classpath), reverting exactly the two properties the fix added - deleteAll/flush moved back to the first statement of importResource, and @Transactional removed - with the guards left intact, plus one probe log line after the delete. Backed up the shipped .class files (md5 7a15d2d92e974af97d2dc9e8ceb2ebd5 and d013bb959d5ca286b8c705a06c34280d), swapped the pre-fix classes into /app/classes and restarted. First attempt through the admin upload endpoint did NOT go red: the probe logged 'PREFIXPROBE after deleteAll count=0 syncActive=true', i.e. the delete really wiped the table mid-import but an ambient transaction on that request path rolled it back. So the same pre-fix build was driven through the startup path instead, with the unimportable CSV installed as the shipped demo file. That went red: 'PREFIXPROBE after deleteAll count=0 syncActive=false' followed by the guard's IllegalStateException, and demo-demo was left with select count(*) = 0 where the shipped build had left 64. Reverted: restored both backed-up .class files and the shipped CSV, confirmed md5s match the originals exactly (7a15d2d9..., d013bb95..., a4fdf2c2f0b514d0a973189203a867e2) and that PREFIXPROBE no longer appears in the class, restarted, and re-ran the positive - demo-demo back to 64, mayo-mayo 463, and the p-colectomy step/option/category-order rows identical to before.

caveats: A header-only antibiotic-pathways.csv (valid header, zero data rows) uploaded to a populated tenant returns 200 and empties it - demo-demo went 6 -> 0 with no error, because the guards only fire when rows were read; the ticket's 'refuses to replace a populated tenant with nothing' does not cover the literally-empty file.

The shipped demo and MGB antibiotic-pathways.csv (which are byte-identical) name 16 procedure identifiers those tenants do not define - p-laparoscopic, p-urology, p-ir, p-ent, p-small-intestine, p-biliary-tract-open and friends - so 23 of 87 rows drop at boot with 'Skipping unknown procedure type' and only 64 pathways land; Mayo imports clean.
The build-time guard everyRowOfTheShippedFileImports seeds procedure types from the pathway file's own Procedure column by design, so it cannot see the demo/MGB drop above.

The pre-fix class used for the red check was HEAD's source with the two fix properties reverted, not a literal checkout of the parent commit, because main's importer has since gained acuity scoping and cache invalidation the parent commit's file does not compile against.

Unrelated noise on the admin upload path: releasing the config-import lock fails on Valkey 8.1 with "ERR unknown command 'DELEX'"; the controller catches and logs it, so the import result is unaffected, but the lock is left to expire by TTL.
Nothing that reads these tables was exercised - resolution and guidance behaviour is out of this ticket's scope.

automation.assessment: AntibioticPathwayCSVImporterTest is already thorough - 50+ cases covering steps/OR/AND/parentheses, None, risk and acuity scoping, duplicate collapse, unknown procedure and unknown drug, the one-comma-short row, the uncovered-scope report, replace-on-reimport, keepsTheConfiguredPathwaysWhenTheFileCannotBeParsed, and a parameterized guard that every row of every shipped file imports. The two gaps found here are exactly the two things that guard cannot see, so the useful additions are narrow.
proposed_tests: Importer test: importing a header-only file into a tenant that already holds pathways must throw rather than delete, asserting the repository still holds the previous rows (fails today - the tenant is silently emptied).

Importer test or build guard: seed procedure types from each tenant's master-procedure-types.csv instead of from the pathway file, and assert every Procedure identifier in the shipped pathway file resolves, so a demo/MGB identifier the tenant does not define fails the build instead of dropping at boot.

Repository/integration test on the startup path: an unimportable antibiotic-pathways.csv leaves the tenant's existing rows committed, locking in that the delete and the write share one transaction rather than relying on an ambient one.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: The shipped files imported on boot for all four tenants and the new tables hold the notation exactly as written - arrows became steps, OR became option positions, AND became ordered category rows, parentheses were stripped, and None became a pathway with no options.

Negative: Uploading an unimportable file to a populated tenant was refused with an explicit error and the tenant kept all 64 of its pathways, on both the admin upload path and the startup path.

Red check: A pre-fix build of the importer that deletes before it parses and holds no transaction was compiled and swapped into the running container, which left the tenant with zero pathways on the same file, then was reverted and the positive re-run.

Automation: Existing importer coverage is strong, so only two narrow cases are proposed - a header-only file must not empty a populated tenant, and shipped pathway rows should be checked against each tenant's own procedure list.

Note: a header-only file currently empties a tenant without error, and 23 of 87 demo and MGB rows name procedures those tenants do not define.
